criteria.label: Marketing Message and SME Identity
criteria.section: Marketing Website Front Page and Functionality
criteria.description: Front page clearly shows the SME's identity, products or services, target customers, value proposition, contact details, and a working call to action.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: Front page fully and clearly communicates the SME's identity, offerings, target customers, value proposition, contact details, and a fully working call to action.

levels.label: Good
levels.description: Most elements are present and clear; one element is missing or slightly unclear.

levels.label: Fair
levels.description: Some key elements are missing or unclear; the marketing message is incomplete.

levels.label: Poor
levels.description: Front page fails to communicate the SME's identity or marketing message.

criteria.label: Visual Design and Usability
criteria.section: Marketing Website Front Page and Functionality
criteria.description: Consistent, readable layout and branding with clear, working navigation and visible feedback on every page.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: Layout, branding, navigation, and feedback are all consistent, polished, and fully functional across all pages.

levels.label: Good
levels.description: Design is mostly consistent and usable; minor issues with feedback or navigation on one page.

levels.label: Fair
levels.description: Layout or branding has noticeable inconsistencies; navigation or feedback is missing on some pages.

levels.label: Poor
levels.description: Design is inconsistent or unusable; navigation is broken or feedback is absent.

criteria.label: Responsive Design and Accessibility Basics
criteria.section: Marketing Website Front Page and Functionality
criteria.description: Layout adapts to desktop, tablet, and phone screens; semantic headings, alt text, labeled form fields, and sufficient contrast.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: Layout fully adapts to all screen sizes; semantic headings, alt text, labeled fields, and contrast requirements are all met.

levels.label: Good
levels.description: Responsive on most screens; one or two accessibility elements are missing or incomplete.

levels.label: Fair
levels.description: Responsive on desktop only or multiple accessibility basics are missing.

levels.label: Poor
levels.description: Layout does not adapt to smaller screens; accessibility basics are largely absent.

criteria.label: Front-Page Features and Interactions
criteria.section: Marketing Website Front Page and Functionality
criteria.description: Links, buttons, calls to action, and PHP-processed features (e.g., inquiry form) work end to end and support the SME's marketing goals.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: All interactive elements and PHP-processed features work end to end and clearly support the SME's marketing goals.

levels.label: Good
levels.description: Most features work; one interactive element or PHP feature has a minor issue.

levels.label: Fair
levels.description: Some features are broken or missing; PHP processing is partially implemented.

levels.label: Poor
levels.description: Most features do not work; PHP-processed features are absent or non-functional.

criteria.label: PHP OOP Design and Code Organization
criteria.section: Marketing Website Front Page and Functionality
criteria.description: Relevant OOP concepts (encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, abstraction) applied purposefully, with organized, well-separated code.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: OOP concepts are applied purposefully and correctly; code is well-organized and clearly separated into logical files or classes.

levels.label: Good
levels.description: Most OOP concepts are correctly applied; code organization is mostly clean with minor issues.

levels.label: Fair
levels.description: OOP concepts are present but misapplied or superficial; code organization needs improvement.

levels.label: Poor
levels.description: OOP concepts are absent or incorrectly applied; code is disorganized.

criteria.label: Forms, Data Handling, Validation, and Security
criteria.section: Marketing Website Front Page and Functionality
criteria.description: Server-side validation, escaped output, safe data handling, and exception handling; PDO prepared statements where applicable.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: Server-side validation, output escaping, exception handling, and PDO prepared statements are all correctly implemented.

levels.label: Good
levels.description: Most security and validation measures are present; one area has a minor gap.

levels.label: Fair
levels.description: Validation or security measures are partial; notable gaps in escaping or prepared statements.

levels.label: Poor
levels.description: Validation and security measures are largely absent.

criteria.label: Reliability and Completeness
criteria.section: Marketing Website Front Page and Functionality
criteria.description: Website runs from the submitted package without major errors and meets the essential project requirements.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: Website runs without errors from the submitted package and meets all essential project requirements.

levels.label: Good
levels.description: Website runs with only minor, non-blocking errors; most requirements are met.

levels.label: Fair
levels.description: Website has noticeable errors that affect some functionality; some requirements are unmet.

levels.label: Poor
levels.description: Website fails to run or has major errors; essential requirements are not met.

criteria.label: Project Overview and SME / Marketing Requirements
criteria.description: Explains the SME, objectives, target audience, scope, and prioritized, testable website requirements.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: SME, objectives, target audience, scope, and prioritized testable requirements are all clearly and completely documented.

levels.label: Good
levels.description: Most elements are well-documented; one element is missing or slightly underdeveloped.

levels.label: Fair
levels.description: Some elements are missing or superficial; requirements are not prioritized or testable.

levels.label: Poor
levels.description: Project overview is largely absent or does not address the SME or requirements.

criteria.label: System Design and Structure
criteria.description: Site map, wireframes or screenshots, class diagram, and folder/namespace structure that match the system actually built.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: Site map, wireframes or screenshots, class diagram, and folder structure are all present and accurately reflect the built system.

levels.label: Good
levels.description: Most design artifacts are present and accurate; one is missing or slightly inconsistent with the built system.

levels.label: Fair
levels.description: Some design artifacts are missing or do not match the built system.

levels.label: Poor
levels.description: Design artifacts are largely absent or do not reflect the actual system.

criteria.label: PHP OOP Implementation Explanation
criteria.description: Accurately explains the classes, relationships, and OOP concepts used, with annotated code excerpts that match the actual code.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: Classes, relationships, and OOP concepts are accurately explained with annotated code excerpts that match the actual implementation.

levels.label: Good

levels.label: Fair
levels.description: Explanation is incomplete or inaccurate in notable areas; code excerpts are missing or do not match.

levels.label: Poor

criteria.label: Data, Forms, Database, and Security Documentation
criteria.description: Describes the form handling, data storage, validation, and security measures that apply to the project (database documentation only if a database is used).

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: Form handling, data storage, validation, and security measures are all clearly and accurately documented.

levels.label: Good
levels.description: Most areas are well-documented; one area has minor gaps.

levels.label: Fair
levels.description: Documentation is partial; some key areas are missing or unclear.

levels.label: Poor

criteria.label: Testing and Evidence
criteria.description: Test cases with expected and actual results, screenshots or logs, and recorded defects and fixes.

levels.description: Test cases with expected and actual results, supporting screenshots or logs, and all recorded defects and fixes are present.

levels.description: Most testing evidence is present; screenshots or defect records have minor gaps.

levels.label: Fair

criteria.label: Organization, Writing, and References
criteria.description: Complete, well-organized, clearly written, and consistently formatted paper with properly acknowledged sources.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: Paper is complete, clearly organized, well-written, consistently formatted, and all sources are properly acknowledged.

levels.label: Good
levels.description: Paper is mostly organized and well-written; minor formatting or reference issues.

levels.label: Fair
levels.description: Organization or writing has noticeable issues; some sources are missing or improperly cited.

levels.label: Poor
levels.description: Paper is disorganized, poorly written, or references are absent.

criteria.label: Organization and Clarity
criteria.description: Presents the project clearly and in logical order, from business context to testing and conclusion.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: Presentation follows a clear and logical order from business context to testing and conclusion; all transitions are smooth.

levels.label: Good
levels.description: Presentation is mostly organized and clear; one section is out of order or unclear.

levels.label: Poor

criteria.label: Live Website Demonstration
criteria.description: Demonstrates the running website's features, navigation, interactions, and at least one invalid-input case.

levels.label: Excellent

levels.label: Good

levels.label: Fair

levels.label: Poor

criteria.label: PHP OOP Technical Understanding
criteria.description: Explains the PHP implementation and accurately discusses the OOP concepts used in the project.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: PHP implementation and all OOP concepts used are accurately explained and clearly connected to the actual project.

levels.label: Good
levels.description: Most OOP concepts are correctly explained; one concept is unclear or slightly inaccurate.

levels.label: Fair
levels.description: OOP concepts are partially explained; notable inaccuracies or missing concepts.

levels.label: Poor
levels.description: PHP OOP explanation is absent or largely incorrect.

criteria.label: Documentation and Design Justification
criteria.description: Justifies key design choices and shows consistency between the website, the code, and the paper.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: Key design choices are clearly justified and the website, code, and paper are fully consistent.

levels.label: Good
levels.description: Most design choices are justified; minor inconsistency between deliverables.

levels.label: Fair
levels.description: Justification is weak; noticeable inconsistencies between the website, code, and paper.

levels.label: Poor
levels.description: No justification provided; deliverables are inconsistent.

criteria.label: Question-and-Answer Defense
criteria.description: Answers questions accurately and shows understanding of the project and its technical decisions.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: All questions are answered accurately and confidently, demonstrating deep understanding of the project and its technical decisions.

levels.label: Good
levels.description: Most questions are answered correctly; one answer is incomplete or slightly off.

levels.label: Fair
levels.description: Answers are partially correct; several questions are unanswered or unclear.

levels.label: Poor
levels.description: Unable to answer most questions; little to no understanding demonstrated.

criteria.label: Delivery, Teamwork, and Time Management
criteria.description: Clear, professional delivery; balanced participation of all members; stays within the allotted time.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: Delivery is clear and professional; all members participate; presentation stays within the allotted time.

levels.label: Good
levels.description: Delivery is mostly professional; minor imbalance in participation or slight overtime.

levels.label: Fair
levels.description: Delivery has noticeable issues; some members do not participate; time is poorly managed.

levels.label: Poor
levels.description: Delivery is unprofessional; participation is unbalanced; time management is poor.

instructions:
UNIVERSIDAD DE DAGUPAN
SCHOOL OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY EDUCATION

Final Project Rubrics — PHP OOP Marketing Website
Total: 100 pts

A. Marketing Website Front Page and Functionality (40 pts)
Evaluates the SME identity and marketing message, visual design and usability, responsive design and accessibility, front-page features and PHP interactions, PHP OOP code quality, forms and security, and overall reliability.

B. Paper Documentation (30 pts)
Evaluates the completeness and accuracy of the project overview, system design artifacts, PHP OOP explanation with annotated code, data/forms/security documentation, testing evidence, and writing quality.

C. Presentation and Demonstration (30 pts)
Evaluates the organization and clarity of the presentation, the live website demo including an invalid-input case, PHP OOP technical understanding, documentation and design justification, Q&A defense, and delivery and teamwork.

Performance Rating Scale
For each criterion, select the performance level that best reflects the group's work based on the defined score ranges.

Final Grade Computation
Final Grade = Sum of scores from Parts A + B + C (out of 100 pts).
